# NPM Improved v1.3.0 — Proxy Host Analytics

NPM Improved v1.3.0 introduces integrated per-proxy-host traffic analytics, with metrics gathered by each NPMi node rather than an external tracking service.

## Traffic and performance visibility

- **Analytics** action in the Proxy Hosts list opens a dedicated host detail screen.
- Requests, HTTP response status families, bandwidth sent/received and error rates.
- Request trend charts for the last hour, day, week, month and 90 days.
- Response-time percentiles (p50/p95/p99) from raw events, hostname/method/top-path breakdowns, device-category estimates and upstream status summaries.
- Paginated request explorer with status filters and sanitized CSV exports of up to 10,000 records.

## Collection without interrupting proxy traffic

- Dedicated JSON-formatted Nginx request logging per Proxy Host.
- Background log reader with durable offsets, partial-line handling and log rotation safeguards.
- Node-local SQLite analytics data, independent of the main proxy configuration database, with seven-day raw event retention and 90-day hourly aggregates by default.
- Nginx host configuration upgrade on first startup to enable analytics on **existing** hosts automatically. Changes are tested with `nginx -t`; unsuccessful activation restores the previous generated host configuration.

## Data privacy and limitations

- The analytics database does not store raw source IP addresses, request query strings, bodies, cookies, authorization headers or full user agents.
- Opaque path segments and common secret identifiers are redacted when recognized; review traditional Nginx access-log retention separately.
- Analytics begin recording after this version is installed; previous traffic cannot be backfilled from unavailable fields.
- Traffic metrics remain **node-local**. NPMX synchronization of proxy configuration does not merge request counts from different servers.
- Unique visitor and country analytics are not collected in this release. Longer-range summaries use hourly rollups, so historical per-path details and latency percentiles are unavailable after raw event expiry.

## Deployment

Available as prebuilt multi-architecture image for Linux amd64 and arm64 through the normal NPM Improved release channel. Existing proxy hosts, TLS certificates, and configuration are retained.

For Docker installations using the Settings → Update manager, update to v1.3.0 when offered, subject to the current NPMX/Shared MySQL coordinated-upgrade restrictions. Back up both `/data` and `/etc/letsencrypt` before upgrading.
